title: Veterans Pension Retroactive Release — How the Amount Is Computed
content:
**Veterans Pension — amount of a retroactive release under a rate adjustment.**

*New monthly rate.* The new monthly rate is the adjustment's annual pension — the most recent rate adjustment on the award — divided by 12 and rounded down to the whole dollar.

*Whether anything is released.* A release has an amount only when the new monthly rate exceeds the gross amount of the most recent monthly payment on the award; when it does not, the release amount is zero.

*Amount.* The release is the new monthly rate times the months owed, less what was already paid for those months, plus the payments returned in those months, less the VA disability compensation paid for months of pension, never below zero and rounded to the cent. In this computation:

- the months owed run from the month of the adjustment's effective date through the current month — the whole months since that effective date plus 1;
- what was already paid is the monthly payments issued in the months owed plus any earlier retroactive release issued in those months, "issued in the months owed" meaning a payment date within that many months before the release;
- a payment returned in the months owed is owed again, and the amount that came back from it is added;
- compensation subtracts nothing.

## Worked example (hypothetical award)

A rate adjustment with an annual pension of 12000 takes effect on the first day of a month that is 2 whole months before today; the most recent monthly payment was 900.00.

1. New monthly rate: 12000 divided by 12 is 1000; it exceeds 900.00, so a release is due.
2. Months owed: 2 whole months plus 1 is 3.
3. Owed at the new rate: 1000 times 3 is 3000.00.
4. Already paid in those months: two monthly payments of 900.00, 1800.00; no earlier retroactive release.
5. Returned in those months: none.
6. Release: 3000.00 less 1800.00 is 1200.00.

Had the new monthly rate been 900 or less, the release would be zero.
